title: Warm late-winter sea one year earlier lowered North Sea kittiwake breeding success also in 2005-2025, not in western UK seas; the June 2023 marine heatwave gave no extra failure
abstract: Question: does the published link between kittiwake breeding success and warm February-March sea surface temperature (SST) one year earlier (North Sea, 1986-2004) continue in new years and other regions, and did the record June 2023 marine heatwave lower seabird breeding success? Data: BTO/JNCC Seabird Monitoring Programme breeding success (20,594 records, 22 species, 1985-2025; kittiwake 1,760 colony-years at 93 colonies) and NOAA OISST v2.1 (HadISST1 for sensitivity). Method: colony fixed-effect regressions by region and period with year-block bootstrap intervals; a forward test of the 1986-2004 slope on 2005-2025; leave-one-year-out residuals for 2023. Results: in the North Sea the slope was -0.135 chicks per pair per 1 C (95% CI -0.235 to -0.015) in 1986-2004 and -0.159 (-0.292 to -0.035) in 2005-2025, about 18% per 1 C. In 2005-2025 it did not change with a linear year term (-0.171) and only the one-year lag was negative (placebo lead +0.07). In 1986-2004 a year term reduced it to -0.058 and the placebo lead was also negative, so the old data alone did not establish the lag. The Irish Sea-Celtic region had no link in either period. The 1986-2004 slope reduced 2005-2025 squared error in eastern colonies by 6.6% (0.5-11.9%) relative to the training mean and by 3.3% (-0.5 to 6.6%) relative to a trailing 5-year mean, and made western forecasts worse. In 2023 (June SST +1.8 C at kittiwake colonies) kittiwake productivity was above the model (+0.09, rank 28 of 40 years); auks were within their normal range. Poor 2023 tern and black-headed gull years did not follow local heat and agree in time with avian influenza. Limitations: SST is a proxy for sandeel supply; no sandeel, fishery, predation or avian influenza data; about 20 effective years per period; non-random monitored colonies. Raw SMP data are not redistributed; a retrieval script is included.

display.caption: Kittiwake breeding success slope on February-March SST one year earlier, by region and period (colony fixed effects, 95% year-bootstrap intervals). The North Sea slope repeats in 2005-2025; the Irish Sea-Celtic region has no link.
Lag profile with a linear year term. In 2005-2025 only the published one-year lag is negative in eastern seas; in 1986-2004 the placebo lead (SST of the next year) is equally negative.

Leave-one-year-out year residuals by species. The June 2023 marine heatwave year (red) is not unusually poor for kittiwake or auks; poor 2023 tern and black-headed gull years coincide with avian influenza.
